sticker_location: The VIN is on a small plate at the lower driver-side corner of the windshield (read it from outside) and on the white certification label on the driver's door pillar. The 10th character is F for a 2015.

parts.label: Hood release lever
parts.where: Inside the car, low on the left kick panel by the driver's left knee. Pull it toward you.

parts.label: Hood support rod
parts.where: Clipped under the front edge of the raised hood. Its free end fits into a slot in the hood to hold it up.

parts.label: Engine oil dipstick
parts.where: At the front of the engine, a yellow loop handle. The tip has L and F dots.

parts.label: Engine oil filler cap
parts.where: On top of the engine's valve cover, marked with an oil-can symbol.

parts.label: Oil drain plug (14 mm)
parts.where: Under the car on the oil pan, the flat metal pan below the engine. 14 mm head with a crush gasket.

parts.label: Oil filter (cartridge)
parts.where: Under the car at the front of the engine, beside the oil pan: a black housing cap pointing straight down. The paper element is inside the cap.

parts.label: Engine coolant reservoir
parts.where: A clear plastic tank under the hood with pink fluid and MAX and MIN lines on its side.

parts.label: Radiator
parts.where: The thin, wide part right behind the front grille, in front of the engine. Look at it only to check it is clean; do not touch it when hot.

parts.label: Brake fluid reservoir
parts.where: At the back of the engine bay on the driver's side, under a small service cover near the windshield. The clear tank has MAX and MIN lines.

parts.label: 12-volt battery
parts.where: A large black box under the hood with two thick cables on top, marked plus and minus.

parts.label: Washer fluid tank
parts.where: A white plastic tank under the hood with a cap showing a windshield and spray symbol.

parts.label: Engine fuse box
parts.where: A black plastic box under the hood with a lift-off lid. Small colored fuses sit inside, and the lid shows what each fuse is for.

parts.label: Cabin air filter
parts.where: Inside the car, hidden behind the glove box on the passenger side, in a flat filter case with a removable cover.

parts.label: Maintenance reset controls
parts.where: The arrow buttons on the steering wheel. They move through menus on the small screen between the dashboard gauges.

parts.label: Windshield wiper blades
parts.where: The two rubber blades resting at the bottom of the windshield, outside the car.

parts.label: Replaceable light bulbs
parts.where: Small bulbs inside the front corner lights and inside the rear light units reached from the trunk. Most other lights are sealed LED units for a dealer.

parts.label: Key fob battery
parts.where: A small flat coin battery hidden inside the car key, reached by removing the key cover.

symptoms: The dash says maintenance is required
It has been about 10,000 miles since my last oil change
My oil looks dark and dirty on the stick

plan.diagnosis: Your 2015 Camry 2.5L is due for fresh oil and a new filter element. It takes 4.6 quarts of 0W-20 with the filter, and the whole job is done from under the front with a drain pan.
replacement_parts: 5 quarts of SAE 0W-20 engine oil (it takes 4.6 with the filter)
Toyota oil filter element 04152-YZZA1 with its O-rings
safety: Never get under a car held up only by a jack. Use ramps or jack stands, and chock the rear wheels.
Let a hot engine cool about 10 minutes; fresh-off-the-road oil can burn.
Take the old oil and filter to an auto parts store for recycling.

steps.instruction: Drive onto ramps, chock the wheels
details: Engine off, parking brake on.
Let a hot engine cool about 10 minutes.
steps.check: Both front wheels sit in the ramp cradles and the rear wheels are chocked.

steps.instruction: Open the hood, loosen the fill cap
details: The release is by your left knee.
Loosening the cap lets the oil drain faster.
steps.check: The hood is propped and the fill cap is loose.

steps.instruction: Drain the oil from the 14 mm plug
details: Turn the plug left, pull it away fast.
Let it drain until it only drips.
Use a new gasket, tighten to 27 ft-lb.
steps.check: The plug is back in with a new gasket and nothing drips.

steps.instruction: Swap the cartridge filter
details: Use the drain tool from the filter box first.
64 mm cap wrench, turn left.
New element and O-ring, oiled. Tighten to 18 ft-lb.
steps.check: The cap is back on snug with the new element inside.

steps.instruction: Pour in 4.4 quarts of 0W-20
details: Use the funnel, go slowly.
Hold the last bit back to check the level first.
steps.check: About 4.4 quarts are in and the cap is back on tight.

steps.instruction: Run it one minute, check for drips
details: Watch the plug and the filter cap.
Engine off, then wait 5 minutes.
steps.check: No drips at the plug or the filter.

steps.instruction: Check the dipstick, top up to F
details: Wipe it, push it fully in, pull again.
Add a little at a time if it's below F.
steps.check: The oil sits between the L and F dots.

plan.aftercare: Reset the oil maintenance reminder (your owner's manual, Maintenance section), then check the dipstick every few fill-ups. Next change in about 10,000 miles or 12 months.

rig_beats.caption: Push it all the way in

symptoms: The oil on my stick is at the low mark
I had to add oil between changes
There is a low oil warning on the dash

plan.diagnosis: Engines use a little oil over time, so the level can drop to the low mark. Topping up slowly to between the marks fixes it unless it keeps dropping fast.
replacement_parts: Engine oil of the same type already in the engine
safety: Park on flat ground and turn the engine off.
Do not touch hot engine parts right after driving.
Do not overfill above the top mark.

steps.instruction: Park level and wait five minutes.
details: Warm engine first, then turn it off.
Five minutes lets oil settle for a true reading.
steps.check: The car is parked flat with engine off.

steps.instruction: Open hood and prop it securely.
details: Pull the release lever by your left foot.
Put the support rod fully into its slot.
steps.check: The hood stays up on its own.

steps.instruction: Pull dipstick out and wipe it clean.
details: Hold a rag under the tip to catch drips.
steps.check: The dipstick tip is wiped clean.

steps.instruction: Push dipstick fully in, then pull out.
details: Look where the oil film ends on the marks.
steps.check: Oil shows at or below the low mark.

steps.instruction: Twist filler cap left and lift off.
details: The cap is on top of the engine.
steps.check: The round filler opening is open.

steps.instruction: Add a little oil and recheck dipstick.
details: Repeat until between low and full marks.
About 1.6 quarts fills low to full.
steps.check: Oil sits between the two marks, not above.

steps.instruction: Turn filler cap clockwise until tight.
details: Push the dipstick fully back in too.
steps.check: Cap is tight and dipstick is fully in.

plan.aftercare: If you add oil often, tell a shop; that can mean a leak or wear.

symptoms: The pink fluid tank is at MIN
My car runs hotter than usual
I see pink puddles under the front

plan.diagnosis: The clear tank should sit between MIN and MAX when the engine is cold. Topping it up fixes a small drop, but a fast drop means a leak.
replacement_parts: Toyota Super Long Life Coolant or matching pink coolant
safety: Only check and open the tank when the engine is fully cold.
Never remove the reservoir cap on a hot engine.
Stop and get help if the temperature warning comes on.

steps.instruction: Park level and let engine cool fully.
details: Cold means the tank feels cool to touch.
Hot coolant can spray and burn.
steps.check: The engine and tank are cool.

steps.instruction: Open hood and prop it securely.
details: Put the support rod fully into its slot.
steps.check: The hood stays up on its own.

steps.instruction: Check pink fluid against MAX and MIN.
details: Read the lines on the side of the clear tank.
Between the lines when cold is correct.
steps.check: You can see fluid at or below MIN.

steps.instruction: Open reservoir cap slowly when cold.
details: Turn it slowly and keep your face away.
steps.check: The cap is off with no steam or spray.

steps.instruction: Pour coolant in slowly to MAX line.
details: Use a clean funnel to avoid spills.
Do not pour past the MAX line.
steps.check: Pink fluid reaches the MAX line.

steps.instruction: Close cap and look for wet leaks.
details: Check hoses and the ground under the front.
Wash any spilled coolant off with water.
steps.check: Cap is tight and no fresh drips show.

plan.aftercare: Recheck the cold level in a few days; a quick drop means a leak.

symptoms: Nothing sprays on my windshield
The washer warning shows on my dash
The wipers just smear the glass

plan.diagnosis: Most no-spray cases are simply an empty washer tank. Filling it with washer fluid, not soapy water, should bring the spray back.
safety: Do not add fluid while the engine is hot or running.
Use only washer fluid, never soapy water or antifreeze.
Keep washer fluid away from children.

steps.instruction: Turn engine off and open hood.
details: Put the support rod fully into its slot.
steps.check: The hood stays up on its own.

steps.instruction: Find white tank with windshield symbol cap.
details: It is a white plastic tank under the hood.
steps.check: You found the tank with the spray symbol.

steps.instruction: Lift cap and pour washer fluid in.
details: Pour slowly with a funnel until nearly full.
In cold areas use fluid rated for winter.
steps.check: Fluid is visible near the top of the tank.

steps.instruction: Press cap down until it seats.
details: Wipe any spill off paint with water.
steps.check: The cap sits flat and snug.

steps.instruction: Close hood and test the spray.
details: Return the rod to its clip before closing.
Pull the washer stalk and watch both jets.
steps.check: Fluid sprays and wipers clear the glass.

plan.aftercare: Top up the washer tank each time you check your oil.

symptoms: Air barely comes out of my vents
The fan sounds loud but blows weak
My windows fog up and stay foggy

plan.diagnosis: Toyota says airflow dropping a lot usually means the cabin filter behind the glove box is clogged. A fresh filter restores normal airflow.
safety: Turn the engine switch fully off first.
Push gently on the glove box; do not force the small clips.
Always run the fan with a filter installed.

steps.instruction: Turn engine off and open glove box.
details: Empty it first so nothing falls out.
steps.check: The glove box is open and empty.

steps.instruction: Squeeze glove box sides and lower it.
details: Push in on the outer side to free the claws.
Slide off the small arm if yours has one.
steps.check: The glove box hangs down out of the way.

steps.instruction: Unlock filter cover and pull it out.
details: The flat cover is right behind the glove box.
steps.check: The filter cover is in your hand.

steps.instruction: Slide filter case out toward you.
details: Note which way the UP marks point.
steps.check: The flat filter case is fully out.

steps.instruction: Swap old filter for new filter.
details: Put UP marks on filter and case pointing up.
steps.check: The clean white filter sits flat in its case.

steps.instruction: Slide case back and refit cover.
details: Push the glove box back until claws click.
steps.check: Cover clicks shut and glove box closes normally.

steps.instruction: Start car and test vent airflow.
details: Turn the fan up and feel each vent.
steps.check: Strong, steady air comes from the vents.

plan.aftercare: Change this filter on schedule, sooner if you drive dusty roads.

symptoms: My car just clicks and won't start
There is white crust on the battery
The battery cable feels loose by hand

plan.diagnosis: White crust or a loose clamp stops power reaching the starter, causing clicks. Cleaning and firmly seating the clamps often restores starting; a dead battery will still need charging or replacement.
safety: Wear safety glasses; battery acid is poisonous and corrosive.
No smoking, sparks, or flames near the battery.
If acid gets in eyes, flush 15 minutes and get medical help.

steps.instruction: Turn everything off and open hood.
details: Put the support rod fully into its slot.
Keep metal tools off both terminals at once.
steps.check: The battery top and both cables are visible.

steps.instruction: Check both clamps for crust and looseness.
details: Try moving each clamp gently by hand.
Look for cracks and loose hold-down parts.
steps.check: You can see crust or feel a clamp move.

steps.instruction: Wipe crust off with baking soda water.
details: Dip a rag, wring it, then wipe the tops.
Keep the mix out of the battery openings.
steps.check: Terminal posts look clean and bright.

steps.instruction: Push each clamp fully down on post.
details: A clamp should sit low, not perched high.
steps.check: Both clamps sit fully down on their posts.

steps.instruction: Tighten each clamp bolt with wrench.
details: Tighten until the clamp cannot twist by hand.
Do not overtighten and crack the clamp.
steps.check: Neither clamp moves when you try to twist it.

steps.instruction: Smear thin grease over both terminals.
details: A thin coat slows new crust forming.
steps.check: Both terminals have a light greasy shine.

steps.instruction: Try starting the engine once.
details: If it only clicks again, the battery is likely dead.
Get it tested or replaced rather than forcing it.
steps.check: The engine starts, or you know the battery needs testing.

plan.aftercare: Glance at the terminals monthly and clean crust early.

symptoms: My power outlet suddenly stopped working
One electrical thing died but others work
The radio went dead all at once

plan.diagnosis: When one electrical item stops suddenly, a small fuse has often blown to protect the wiring. Replacing it with the exact same rating usually restores power.
tools: Fuse puller tool from the fuse box lid
replacement_parts: Fuse with the same amperage rating as the old one
safety: Turn the engine switch off before touching fuses.
Never use a higher-rated fuse or a wire instead.
If the new fuse blows again, get the car inspected.

steps.instruction: Turn engine off and open hood.
details: Put the support rod fully into its slot.
steps.check: The hood stays up on its own.

steps.instruction: Push tabs and lift fuse box lid.
details: The lid map shows what each fuse feeds.
Some dead items use the cabin fuse box instead.
steps.check: Rows of small colored fuses are visible.

steps.instruction: Pull suspect fuse out with puller tool.
details: Use the small white puller clipped in the lid.
Only pull the fuse for the dead item.
steps.check: The fuse is out in your hand.

steps.instruction: Look through fuse for broken strip.
details: A blown fuse shows a gap or dark burn.
A good fuse shows one unbroken strip.
steps.check: You can see the strip is broken.

steps.instruction: Push in new fuse of same rating.
details: Match the number printed on top exactly.
Push until it sits level with its neighbors.
steps.check: The new fuse sits flat and firm.

steps.instruction: Refit lid and test dead item.
details: Make sure both lid tabs click securely.
steps.check: The lid is shut and the item works again.

plan.aftercare: Keep spare fuses of the listed ratings in the glove box.
